questions.q: A contoured survey map of a region in West Africa is drawn to a scale of $1:50,000$. If the distance between two settlements on the map is measured to be $4 \text{ cm}$, what is the actual distance between these two settlements on the ground?
questions.explain:
To calculate the actual distance on the ground, use the formula:

$$\text{Actual Distance} = \text{Map Distance} \times \text{Scale Factor}$$

Given the map distance is $4 \text{ cm}$ and the scale is $1:50,000$:

$$\text{Ground Distance} = 4 \text{ cm} \times 50,000 = 200,000 \text{ cm}$$

To convert centimeters to kilometers, divide by $100,000$ (since $100,000 \text{ cm} = 1 \text{ km}$):

$$\frac{200,000 \text{ cm}}{100,000 \text{ cm/km}} = 2 \text{ km}$$

questions.q: On a topographical map, a cross-profile analysis reveals that the elevation of point X on a spur is $400 \text{ m}$ above sea level, while point Y in a nearby valley is $200 \text{ m}$ above sea level. If the horizontal distance (horizontal equivalent) between X and Y is $4 \text{ km}$, what is the gradient of the slope connecting them?
questions.explain:
Gradient is calculated using the formula:

$$\text{Gradient} = \frac{\text{Vertical Interval (V.I.)}}{\text{Horizontal Equivalent (H.E.)}}$$

**Step 1:** Calculate Vertical Interval:
$$\text{V.I.} = 400 \text{ m} - 200 \text{ m} = 200 \text{ m}$$

**Step 2:** Convert Horizontal Equivalent to matching units (meters):
$$\text{H.E.} = 4 \text{ km} = 4,000 \text{ m}$$

**Step 3:** Calculate Gradient:
$$\text{Gradient} = \frac{200}{4,000} = \frac{1}{20}$$

This is expressed as a ratio of **$1 \text{ in } 20$**.

questions.q:
Consider the contour pattern depicted below, representing a common landform in physical geography:

<svg viewBox="0 0 200 200" width="250" height="250" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <!-- Contour lines pointing towards lower ground -->
  <path d="M 50 50 L 100 100 L 150 50" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="100" y="115" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#111">300m</text>
  
  <path d="M 30 70 L 100 140 L 170 70" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="100" y="155" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#111">200m</text>
  
  <path d="M 10 90 L 100 180 L 190 90" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="100" y="195" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#111">100m</text>
</svg>

Which of the following physical features does this V-shaped pattern, pointing towards the lower elevation, represent?
questions.explain:
On a contoured survey map, V-shaped contour lines pointing **away** from the higher ground and **towards** the lower ground indicate a **spur** (a prominent ridge descending from a highland). Conversely, if the V-shapes point *up* towards higher elevations, they signify a **valley**.

Since the vertex of the $100\text{m}$ line (lower ground) juts outward from the $300\text{m}$ area, this confirms it is a spur.

questions.q: During a fieldwork traverse using a prismatic compass, a student sights a distant communication mast from a village and records a forward bearing of $045^\circ$. What will be the backward bearing of the village if sighted from the communication mast?
questions.explain:
To find the backward (or back) bearing from a forward bearing, you apply a simple rule based on whether the forward bearing is less than or greater than $180^\circ$:

- If $\text{Forward Bearing} < 180^\circ$, add $180^\circ$.
- If $\text{Forward Bearing} > 180^\circ$, subtract $180^\circ$.

Since the forward bearing is $045^\circ$ (which is $< 180^\circ$):
$$\text{Backward Bearing} = 045^\circ + 180^\circ = 225^\circ$$

questions.q: When analyzing inter-visibility between two observation points on a topographical map of a region in West Africa, which of the following conditions definitively implies that the two points are **NOT** inter-visible?
options: The horizontal distance separating the points is greater than $5 \text{ km}$.
An intervening contour feature on the line of sight has an elevation higher than both observation points.
The two points are located on contour lines of differing numerical values.
A river channel flows between the two points perpendicularly to the line of sight.
questions.explain:
**Inter-visibility** refers to whether one point can be seen from another on the ground. 

If you draw a cross-profile between two points, a line of sight is drawn connecting them. If the physical landform (e.g., a hill or spur with higher elevation contours) rises above this line of sight, the visual connection is blocked, making them **not** inter-visible. Distance (A), unequal elevations (C), and intervening valleys or rivers (D) do not inherently block the line of sight.
